subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool implementation now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The requested capability is real, but this PR changes core config, model-facing tool parameters, message delivery, session state, and Gateway security boundaries in ways that need maintainer product/security intent before repair can be judged sufficient.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR paused and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43605 plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 to settle peer identity, scopes, URL policy, and delivery guarantees before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer PR
options.body: Explicitly accept `gateway.peers` as the near-term shape and require this branch or a replacement to fix the protocol/security findings, rebase cleanly, and provide real multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer to external bridges
options.body: If core federation is out of scope for now, document supported plugin/MCP/HTTP bridge patterns and close implementation PRs that add core peer routing.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR paused and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43605 plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 to settle peer identity, scopes, URL policy, and delivery guarantees before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses session tools, Gateway URL security, and protocol shape, and Peter's history is strongest on the original session tool and URL-restriction boundaries.
